description: The line plot illustrates how the performance metric minADE₂₀ (lower is better) changes as the “Ratio” of the in-context pool size varies from 0.0 to 1.0, with five different fine-tuning methods compared: TrajCL (blue circles, solid line), Head Tuning (orange circles, solid line), FT (green circles, solid line), LoRA 16 (red circles, solid line), and LoRA 64 (purple circles, solid line). The x-axis, labeled “Ratio,” spans from 0.0 to 1.0 in linear increments of 0.2. The y-axis, labeled “minADE₂₀ (←),” ranges from 0.50 to 0.80 in increments of 0.05, with the arrow indicating that lower values are preferable. Head Tuning starts at approximately 0.79 at Ratio=0.0 and steadily declines to about 0.68 at Ratio=1.0. LoRA 64 begins near 0.75, drops sharply to ~0.70 at Ratio=0.2, then gradually decreases to ~0.60 at Ratio=1.0. LoRA 16 starts at ~0.74, declines to ~0.67 at Ratio=0.2, and continues falling to ~0.60 at Ratio=1.0. FT begins at ~0.68, drops steeply to ~0.58 at Ratio=0.6, and plateaus near 0.53 at Ratio=1.0. TrajCL remains relatively flat, starting at ~0.61, dipping slightly to ~0.59 at Ratio=0.4, then rising back to ~0.60 at Ratio=1.0. All methods show improved performance (lower minADE₂₀) as the ratio increases, though at different rates and final performance levels.
